newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crude oil jumps in Asia on Iraq-U.S. tension.
newsitem.headline: Crude oil jumps in Asia on Iraq-U.S. tension.

text.p: NYMEX light crude oil prices on the ACCESS after-hours system surged in early Asia trade on Tuesday in response to heightening tension between the United States and Iraq, traders said.
At 9.16 a.m. (0016 GMT), October NYMEX light crude was traded at $23.30, up $1.05 from the Friday New York close.
NYMEX was closed on Monday for the Labor Day holiday.
London Brent futures closed up a sharp $1.21 at $21.99 on Monday, spurred by tension in northern Iraq and a delay in possible Iraqi oil exports.
"If the current momentum keeps up, NYMEX October could rise above $24.00," a trader said.
By Monday, Iraqi troops were reported by United Nations personnel to have evacuated the Iraqi Kurdistan city of Arbil.
However, the United States dismissed the Iraqi redeployment, saying troops were still arrayed around Arbil.
CNN reported on Tuesday that U.S. Air Force B-52 bombers carrying cruise missiles were in the air but that it was unknown if they were headed for Iraq.
They took off from bases in Guam, CNN reported, citing a Pentagon source. CNN reported there was no confirmation of any attack taking place.
